metadata.description: Diagnoses common computer hardware and software issues

rules.explanation: If the system is completely unresponsive with no lights, the power cable is the first suspect.
If the cable is secure but there's still no power, verify the wall outlet works.
Lights indicate the PC has power. A black screen suggests a display issue.
Beep codes often indicate hardware initialization failures, commonly RAM.
Slow performance is often caused by a rogue process consuming CPU.
If CPU usage is normal, a full hard drive can cause significant slowdowns.

questions.system_dead: Does the computer show absolutely no signs of life (no fans, no lights)?
questions.no_lights: Are there no LED lights visible on the case or motherboard?
questions.cable_secure: Is the power cable firmly plugged into both the wall and the PC?
questions.lights_on: Do you see fans spinning or LED lights on the case?
questions.screen_black: Is the monitor screen completely black?
questions.no_beeps: Is the computer silent (no beep sounds on startup)?
questions.hear_beeps: Do you hear a series of beeping sounds?
questions.pc_boots: Does the computer boot into the operating system?
questions.system_slow: Is the system performance noticeably slower than usual?
questions.cpu_normal: Is the CPU usage below 50% in Task Manager?

solutions.check_power_cable: Please check that the power cable is securely connected.
solutions.check_outlet: Try plugging another device into the same outlet to verify it has power. You may need a replacement PSU.
solutions.check_monitor_cable: Ensure the monitor cable (HDMI/DisplayPort) is tightly connected to the GPU.
solutions.check_ram_seating: Reseat the RAM sticks: Open the case, remove RAM, and click it back in firmly.
solutions.check_high_cpu: Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) and close any programs using high CPU.
solutions.check_disk_space: Check your C: drive. If it's red/full, delete temporary files or uninstall unused games.
